newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk court jails Kurd politicians for rebel links.
newsitem.headline: Turk court jails Kurd politicians for rebel links.

text.p: A court on Wednesday sentenced more than 30 leading members of Turkey's main Kurdish party to up to six years in jail for aiding Kurdish separatist rebels, court officials said.
Murat Bozlak, the leader of the pro-Kurdish People's Democracy Party (HADEP), was among those jailed, officials at the Ankara State Security Court said.

Bozlak was among 47 people arrested after a HADEP congres in June last year when the Turkish flag was torn down and replaced with banners of the rebel Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK). The youth who torn down the flag was jailed for 22 1/2 years, judge Orhan Karadeniz said.
"A close link was discovered between HADEP and the illegal terror organisation PKK," Karadeniz told the court.

HADEP was formed in 1994 after another Kurdish party was closed by the constitutional court for alleged separatism and 13 of its deputies were expelled from parliament. Six of that party's MPs were jailed for links with the rebels.

More than 24,000 people have died in the 13 years of conflict between the Turkish security forces and PKK rebels who are fighting for independence or autonomy in the mainly Kurdish southeast of Turkey.
